metaDescription: Six manual citrus juicers compared: cast iron lever presses, a stainless lever squeezer, reamer cups and a hinged hand juicer, ranked on leverage and cleanup.
introParagraphs: A manual citrus juicer has no motor, no cord and nothing to burn out, which is exactly why people keep buying them. The six here come in three families: heavy cast iron presses like the CO-Z and TONGCHANT, a lever squeezer with a 4.3 inch bowl from Sopito, and compact tools such as the ChefVille reamer cup, the Etinslant stainless reamer and the Zulay hinged 2-in-1.

We compared them on how they multiply your effort, how much juice they hold, what size fruit they accept and how many parts have to be washed. A cast iron press does the most with the least effort but is heavy, a hinged squeezer is the lightest but needs a firm grip, and a reamer cup sits in between.
Because manual juicers have no wattage to compare, the choices come down to leverage, build and storage. Use the tables near the end to match a tool to your fruit, your counter and your hands.

products.name: CO-Z Commercial Grade Cast Iron Citrus Juicer
products.description:
The CO-Z press is the most substantial manual juicer on this list, built from 15 pounds of reinforced cast iron that the listing says withstands over 2300 psi. A long ergonomic lever handle with a rubber grip multiplies your pull, and the fruit contact parts are 304 stainless steel. The listing even says it can press pomegranates, which tells you how much leverage is on offer.

What that means in practice is that a half orange gives up its juice in a single steady pull, with little squeezing from your hand. Weight is the cost. A 15 pound press is not something you move casually, and it needs a permanent spot on the counter or a low shelf. The stainless cone and strainer lift out for washing, but the iron body should be wiped dry to avoid rust.

Compared with the Etinslant, it is far heavier but far less effortful. Compared with the Sopito, it stays planted on the counter while the Sopito has to be held, so both of your hands are free to pull. It is the best pick for someone who juices several fruit every day. Place a folded cloth under the base if your counter is delicate, and leave a small gap behind it so the lever can swing fully.
products.bestFor: Daily juicers who want the most leverage for the least effort.
pros: 15 lb cast iron body stays steady
Long rubber grip lever multiplies your pull
304 stainless cone and strainer
Presses oranges, grapefruit and even pomegranates
cons: Too heavy to move or store casually
Iron body must be wiped dry to avoid rust

products.name: TONGCHANT Cast Iron Manual Juicer 15 Inch
products.description:
The TONGCHANT is a 15 inch tall cast iron hand press with a solid body and a heavy base for stability. A long handle provides leverage, the funnel is food grade 304 stainless steel, and the removable strainer catches seeds and pulp. The listing says you can wash it by hand or put the removable parts in the dishwasher.

Height is its defining trait. A tall press gives the lever a long arc, which means smoother force on the fruit and less stop and start in the motion, but it also needs headroom under wall cabinets, and 15 inches is a lot for some kitchens. The heavy base keeps it from tipping during a hard pull. As with any cast iron tool, keep the iron dry and wipe it after use.

Compared with the CO-Z, it has similar construction but fewer published details about pressure and weight, so treat the comparison as approximate. Compared with the Zulay hinged squeezer, it handles whole oranges. It suits households that juice breakfast oranges and want a long lever. Test the clearance under your cabinets before you commit, because a tall press with the lever raised needs more room than its resting height suggests.
products.bestFor: Breakfast oranges with a long, smooth lever stroke.
pros: Heavy base resists tipping during a pull
Long handle gives a smooth arc
Removable 304 stainless funnel and strainer
Parts can go in the dishwasher
cons: Less published detail on pressure rating

products.name: Sopito Stainless Steel Manual Juice Press
products.description:
The Sopito is a stainless steel hand press with an extended ergonomic lever handle and a bowl that is 4.3 inches wide. The listing notes that most oranges measure 2.6 to 3.5 inches across, so the bowl accommodates nearly any citrus, and a built in cone aims to improve extraction. It is described as dishwasher safe.

The longer handle gives you extra leverage compared with a short hinged squeezer, but it is still a hand held tool rather than a bolted down press, so you need to hold the base with one hand and push with the other. That makes it much lighter and easier to store than the cast iron presses, but less effortless on grapefruit. It is also a single piece of metal, which keeps cleanup simple.

Compared with the Zulay 2-in-1, it has a larger bowl and a longer lever. Compared with the CO-Z, it trades leverage for portability. It is a good middle choice. A tool like this can live in a drawer, come out for Sunday brunch and go back in, without ever asking for a power outlet or a permanent counter spot.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want more leverage without a heavy press.
pros: 4.3 inch bowl accepts nearly any orange
Extended lever gives extra leverage
Dishwasher safe stainless construction
Much lighter than cast iron presses
cons: Held in the hand, so still needs a firm grip
Less leverage than a bolted down press

products.name: ChefVille 4 in 1 Manual Orange Juicer

specList.label: Cup
specList.value: 16.9 oz, 40% larger than a typical 12 oz

products.description:
The ChefVille reamer cup holds 16.9 ounces, which the listing says is 40 percent larger than a typical 12 ounce cup, and comes with two juicing heads, a larger one for oranges and grapefruit and a smaller one for lemons and limes. An unusual side grip design, with a detachable handle, means you squeeze with the fruit rather than pressing a lever.

The big cup means fewer pauses to pour, and the measuring scale helps with recipes. The reamer approach requires a twisting motion, which is a different feel from a lever, and it can take longer per fruit than a press. The detachable handle makes washing and storage easier, though it also adds a part that can go missing. Keep it clipped in the same drawer as the cup, and it will be there when you need it.

Compared with the Etinslant, it offers two heads and a larger cup. Compared with the cast iron presses, it takes minimal space, and costs far less to replace if you ever outgrow it. It suits people who want a low cost, simple tool with decent capacity. The large cup also doubles as a small pitcher, so you can juice, measure and pour from the same piece.
products.bestFor: Cooks who juice a few fruits for lemonade or dressings.
pros: 16.9 oz cup is larger than typical 12 oz cups
Two reamer heads for small and large fruit
Side grip design with detachable handle
Compact and easy to store
cons: Twisting reamer takes more time per fruit
Detachable handle is one more piece to track

products.name: Etinslant 304 Stainless Steel Manual Citrus Juicer
products.description:
The Etinslant is an all stainless reamer with a rotating cone and a juice container that has two sided handles for a secure grip and two spouts for easy pouring. The listing says the steel is robust 304, also called 18/8, anti rust and resistant to citrus acid, with slits in the sieve to strain seeds, and that it is dishwasher safe.

Because it is a reamer, you hold half a fruit against the cone and twist, a motion that feels natural for oranges and lemons. The two handled container is nicer to pour from than a simple cup. The cost is effort: a reamer relies on your wrist, so a bag of oranges will tire the hand faster than a lever press.

Compared with the ChefVille, it is all metal rather than plastic. Compared with the Sopito, it has a container rather than a bowl you squeeze directly. That container means a sit down, twist and pour routine that suits slow weekend mornings. It suits cooks who want an easy to clean, non plastic tool. If you rinse the cone straight away, pulp rarely dries into the slits and the dishwasher does the rest.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want an all stainless, dishwasher safe tool.
pros: All 304 (18/8) stainless steel
Two sided handles and two spouts for easy pouring
Slit sieve strains seeds
Dishwasher safe

products.name: Zulay Kitchen Metal 2 in 1 Lemon Lime Squeezer
products.description:
The Zulay 2 in 1 is a hinged hand squeezer that handles lemons and limes in two bowl sizes. The listing calls the bowls sturdy and heavy duty, made from aluminum with a food grade coating, and highlights that it takes no power, no batteries and little room in a drawer.

Compactness is the point. It slips into a utensil drawer and juices a lemon in seconds, which makes it the right tool for the occasional wedge for fish, tea or a cocktail. It is not intended for large oranges or grapefruit, and the leverage is modest, so a firm grip is needed. Squeeze with the cut side facing down, so the juice runs out through the holes and not over your hand. The coating should be treated gently, avoiding abrasive scrubbing.

Compared with the Sopito, it is smaller and cheaper, though you give up bowl width. Compared with the cast iron presses, it is a different class of tool. It suits cooks who need a little juice, not a pitcher. Hold the squeezer over a small bowl rather than directly over the dish, so any seeds that escape can be fished out easily.
products.bestFor: Lemons and limes for everyday cooking and drinks.
pros: Two bowl sizes for lemons and limes
Fits in a utensil drawer
No power or batteries needed
Lowest cost among the squeezers
cons: Not meant for large oranges or grapefruit
Coated aluminum should not be scrubbed hard

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cast iron presses like the CO-Z multiply your pull so a single steady motion extracts a half orange. A hand held lever such as the Sopito gives some leverage, while reamers such as the Etinslant and ChefVille rely on twisting. If your hands tire easily, favour a bolted down lever with a long arm. Light squeezers suit small jobs. In general, the more fruit you juice at a time, the more a press pays you back, because the last half of a bag of oranges is where hand squeezers start to wear you out.

Bowl width limits what fits. The Sopito bowl is 4.3 inches wide, which fits most oranges that run 2.6 to 3.5 inches, while the Zulay 2 in 1 targets lemons and limes. The ChefVille's two heads split the difference. If you juice grapefruit, choose a wide bowl and a long lever. Grapefruit halves are thick and heavy, and a narrow bowl forces you to squeeze unevenly, leaving juice behind in the membranes.

The CO-Z weighs 15 pounds and stays put on the counter, the TONGCHANT has a heavy base, and the squeezers weigh almost nothing. A heavy press resists tipping but is harder to store. If you will move it often, choose a lighter tool. Anything over about ten pounds is awkward to lift from a low cabinet, and the CO-Z at 15 pounds is best left on the counter for good.

Citrus acid can react with some metals. The Etinslant and CO-Z list 304 stainless steel, which resists acid, and the Zulay uses a food grade coating over aluminum. Rinse acid off coated parts promptly and avoid harsh scrubbing. Cast iron bodies should stay dry. If a press is shipped with a painted or enamelled body, avoid soaking it, since water seeping into joints is what starts corrosion.

The ChefVille holds 16.9 ounces, the Etinslant has two spouts and a slit sieve, and the TONGCHANT has a removable strainer. A built in strainer keeps seeds out of the glass. If you want pulp free juice, check the strainer fineness. Removable strainers, as on the TONGCHANT, are easier to rinse than fixed ones, which can trap fibres in tight corners.

Removable stainless parts rinse fast and many are dishwasher safe, as for the Sopito, Etinslant and TONGCHANT. Cast iron bodies are wiped. Hinged squeezers need only a rinse, but check that no pulp is trapped in the hinge, because that is the spot that gets sticky and slow to open if left. Think about drawer space for small tools and cabinet space for presses. A tool that lives where you can reach it in one movement is the one you will use on a weekday morning, so be honest about your kitchen layout.

howWeEvaluated.title: Leverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared mechanisms: cast iron levers on the CO-Z and TONGCHANT, a hand held lever on the Sopito, twisting reamers on the Etinslant and ChefVille and a hinged squeezer on the Zulay.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fruit range
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted stated sizes, such as the Sopito 4.3 inch bowl and the ChefVille two head design, and the Zulay focus on lemons and limes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded 304 stainless claims for the CO-Z, TONGCHANT, Etinslant and Sopito, and the coated aluminum of the Zulay. Because we evaluate from listings and buyer feedback rather than hands on testing, we credit material claims cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed the 15 lb CO-Z and heavy based TONGCHANT against lighter tools in drawer space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The CO-Z leads on leverage, the TONGCHANT on height, the Sopito on portability, the ChefVille on cup size, the Etinslant on stainless build and the Zulay on compactness.

faq.a: Yes if you value silence, durability and simple cleanup. They cost less than most electric machines and have no motor to fail. They ask for more effort than electric models, but in return they are silent, cordless and usually last for years.

faq.q: How do I get more juice?
faq.a: Roll the fruit on the counter, use room temperature fruit and press slowly. Firm, heavy fruit with thin skin tends to hold more juice than light, thick skinned fruit of the same size. Cut across the segments rather than through the stem, which exposes more of the flesh to the cone. Squeeze until the flesh looks dry. Then flip the rind inside out if the tool allows, because a second squeeze often releases a little more juice.

Cast iron can rust if left wet. Wipe the body dry after use. A light coat of food safe oil on bare iron in humid climates helps if you only use the press occasionally. The stainless parts that touch the fruit are separate and rinse clean.

faq.q: Can I put them in the dishwasher?
faq.a: The Sopito, Etinslant and TONGCHANT parts are listed as dishwasher safe. Check each listing. Coated aluminum should be washed gently, and dried afterwards, so the finish stays intact.

Check the bowl width. The Sopito's 4.3 inch bowl fits most oranges. Hinged squeezers are best for lemons and limes. For oranges and grapefruit, step up to a bowl or press that is clearly wider than the fruit.

faq.q: Which is gentlest on tired hands?
faq.a: A cast iron press with a long handle, such as the CO-Z, needs the least grip. Reamers need wrist twisting and small squeezers need a firm hand. If you have a medical concern, ask a doctor or occupational therapist.
